description: Where the weather comes from, how often it is asked for, and the numbers a reading is read against. A SEPARATE SINGLE FROM ERPNext MCP Settings, deliberately: that document is the MCP endpoint's own control panel and this one is an operational configuration a farm manager should be able to open without being handed the tool switches and the bearer token. `enabled` is the kill switch for the whole weather surface — off, the scheduled sweep returns immediately, the two mutating tools refuse by name, and nothing on this site makes an outbound request.

fields.description: The master switch for everything weather. Off means the scheduled sweep returns without a query, fetch_weather_now and backfill_weather_for_shift refuse and say why, and this site makes no outbound request to anybody. Ships ON, because a shift with no timeline is the failure this release exists to fix and a switch that has to be found before anything works is a support call rather than a safeguard.
fields.label: Enabled

fields.description: How old the most recent reading on an open shift must be before the sweep fetches another. THE CRON RUNS EVERY FIFTEEN MINUTES WHATEVER THIS SAYS — a Frappe cron expression is a static string in hooks.py and cannot be rewritten from a form — so this is a floor rather than a clock. Raising it to 60 gets one reading an hour; lowering it below 15 changes nothing, because the sweep cannot run more often than it is scheduled to. Raising it is the change most operations actually want.
fields.label: Fetch Interval (minutes)

fields.description: How long a fetched reading is reused for the same place before Open-Meteo is asked again. Two shifts on adjacent blocks round to the same coordinates and would otherwise be two identical requests a second apart. Open-Meteo is free and has no API key, which is a reason to be more careful with it rather than less: the only thing standing between this app and a rate limit is this number.
fields.label: Cache TTL (seconds)

fields.description: How long one HTTP call may take before it is abandoned. Ten seconds, because the caller is a scheduled job sharing a worker with the rest of the site's background work and a weather service that hung would hold that worker for as long as the far end felt like holding it.
fields.label: HTTP Timeout (seconds)

fields.description: Air temperature at which a reading writes a Threshold Crossed compliance event onto the shift. OAR 437-004-1131's own number. A FIELD RATHER THAN A CONSTANT because Oregon has changed it before and will again, and a threshold that lives in code is a threshold that needs a release.
fields.label: Heat Threshold — Temp (°F)

fields.description: Heat index at which a reading writes a Threshold Crossed event. THE NUMBER THE RULE ACTUALLY TURNS ON — heat index is temperature and humidity together, and 88 °F at 70% humidity is a 100 °F heat index and a shift somebody could be cited over while the thermometer reads comfortably.
fields.label: Heat Threshold — Heat Index (°F)

fields.description: Wind speed at which a reading on a SPRAY shift writes a Threshold Crossed event. Nearly every pesticide label sets a maximum and it is the first thing an Oregon Department of Agriculture drift investigation asks for. It fires on Spray shifts only: fifteen miles an hour during a prune is weather, and during an application it is a decision somebody has to make.
fields.label: Wind Threshold — Spray Block (mph)

fields.description: Entities whose thresholds differ from the three above. Empty is the ordinary case. Every column on a row is nullable and null falls back to the parent, so a row that exists to lower one entity's wind limit leaves its heat limits alone. One row per company — a second is refused, because two answers to 'what is this company's threshold' is one nobody can defend.
fields.label: Per-Company Overrides

fields.description: Current conditions and forecast. Configurable because an operation running a self-hosted Open-Meteo, or a mirror inside a network that does not reach the public internet, is a real deployment — and because an endpoint hard-coded in a release is an endpoint nobody can move when the far end does.
fields.label: Current / Forecast URL

fields.description: The historical reanalysis, which is what backfill_weather_for_shift reads. A DIFFERENT HOST from the forecast API and not an accident of Open-Meteo's naming — the archive is a distinct dataset with its own lag, and a shift that ended this morning may not be in it yet.
fields.label: Archive URL

fields.description: Turns a place name into coordinates, for the shifts whose farm_location_gps is 'Milton-Freewater, OR' rather than a pair of numbers. Resolved once per distinct string and cached, because a block name does not move.
fields.label: Geocoding URL
Block Forecasts for Work Timing
fields.description: v0.239.0. On: Work Timing rules may read Open-Meteo's 16-day and 48-hour forecast for a task's block (one request per H3 cell, cached two hours). Off: every weather check reads 'no data' and holds, saying why. Desk only.

name: Weather Settings
